bumpRationale: Patch, security: Base44 security scan finding 'Evitar el uso no autorizado de créditos' (High). The browser called the credit-consuming integrations Core.SendEmail (notifications/service.js, Asistencia.jsx, CrearBitacora.jsx) and Core.InvokeLLM (CrearBitacora.jsx, support/aiIntake.js) directly with client-built prompts, bodies and recipients. Moved all five behind three new backend functions — sendNotificationEmail (server-rendered templates, caller and recipient re-derived from UserProfile), notifyParents (absence/diary emails built from the stored record, absence idempotent via parent_notified, diary limited to 10 min after creation) and aiAssist (prompts built server-side). UploadFile and the Lumi agent are unchanged. Verified: lint (validate:functions 9/40), typecheck, build, validate:rls, test (278/278), test:permissions (23/23). deno not available in this sandbox — the three functions get their first real run on deploy.
previousBumpRationale_1_7_14: Patch, security/ops: scheduled full-review audit pass. Pre-flight: repo clean, HEAD == origin/main (4c516a8), zero open PRs, no stray audit branches, no secrets in tree. Full verification suite green before touching anything: lint (incl. validate:functions, 6/40), typecheck, build, validate:rls (32 entities), test (276/276), test:permissions (23/23), release:gate, npm audit (0 vulnerabilities — no new dependency advisory this cycle). Two real findings, both closed: (1) DOCUMENTATION DRIFT — every audit since 2026-09-10 (module 18's retirement commit, then the 08-31/09-07/09-14 passes) kept repeating that the module-14 finding (exportSchoolData/governRoleChange picking the caller's UserProfile via their own unordered .find(ADMIN && ACTIVE) instead of the deterministic selectCurrentUserProfile order) was still open. It was not: commit 4ec5e0c (2026-09-10, part of module 18's since-reverted school-switcher work) already added the '-created_date' sort to both functions, and the later retirement commit (d6f217d) never touched entry.ts — its own commit message asserted the finding was still open without rechecking. (2) PRODUCTION DEPLOY DRIFT, the more serious one — with Base44 MCP access available in this session for the first time, comparing the live app's sandbox source by CONTENT (this app's own established method, not by hash) against git HEAD found the deployed functions/frontend bundle frozen at package.json 1.7.10 / react-router-dom ^6.26.0, while the repo had moved to 1.7.13 with the router v7 CVE fix from 2026-08-31 — meaning that fix, and every change after it, had never actually reached production users for close to a month. The app-checkpoint history confirms it: no deploy recorded between 2026-08-24T20:43 and this pass. Root cause: Base44's own side had diverged (a base44-builder[bot] RLS-recommendation commit plus direct in-app edits by prior sessions), so GitHub sync silently stopped applying new commits. Fixed by pulling from GitHub (hit a merge conflict scoped to package-lock.json only), resolving it via Base44's own conflict-resolution run (landed as merge commit 504ca94 on main — diff limited to bumping @base44/sdk 0.8.44->0.8.48 and @base44/vite-plugin 1.0.31->1.0.41, Base44's own tooling, nothing else), and deploying: the new checkpoint's git_commit_hash (504ca94) and last_deployed_at now match. Spot-checked one entity's LIVE deployed RLS (SchoolSubscription, chosen because it had a documented 08-26 regression/fix) via list_entity_schemas and confirmed the corrected $and-wrapped rule is already live — entity schema deploys evidently went through a separate, unaffected path (prior sessions' direct update_entity_schema calls), so this was a code/functions-bundle deploy gap specifically, not an RLS gap. Did not re-verify all 32 entities' live schema individually this pass (same scope boundary validate:rls/module-14 have always drawn — this was a targeted spot-check of the one entity with known history, not an exhaustive re-audit). No entity, RLS, permission, or route-access code touched by hand; the only non-doc/version diff on main is the bot-resolved package.json/package-lock.json bump already described. Verified again after the redeploy: lint, typecheck, build, validate:rls (32 entities), test (276/276), test:permissions (23/23), release:gate, npm audit (0 vulnerabilities) all pass.

Ran the full verification suite fresh — npm run lint (incl. validate:functions, 6/40 endpoints), npm run typecheck, npm run build, npm run validate:rls (32 entities), npm test (276/276), npm run test:permissions (23/23), npm run release:gate — all green before touching anything. npm audit surfaced exactly one new advisory since 1.7.12 (2026-09-07): js-yaml (high — GHSA-2883-xcg3-v3hh, unbounded CPU use via maxTotalMergeKeys on an untrusted YAML merge). It is a transitive devDependency of eslint (via @eslint/eslintrc) — a build-time linter dependency, never bundled into the app users load — same risk shape as every dependency advisory closed in 1.7.9/1.7.11/1.7.12. Closed with npm audit fix (js-yaml 4.3.1 -> 4.3.2, lockfile-only, no code change, no major bump); re-ran the full suite above afterward, all still green; npm audit now reports 0 vulnerabilities. No new isolation finding: this pass did not re-walk the deployed Base44 RLS schema (that needs the Base44 MCP against production credentials, per module 14/the 2026-08-31 audit's own scope note) or re-derive tenant isolation from scratch four days after the 2026-09-10 module-18 pass already did so — it re-verified that the file-level RLS shape and the full test/build/lint suite still hold, which is what changed (a fresh npm install pulling in a newer transitive js-yaml). The module-14 finding already on record (exportSchoolData:43 / governRoleChange:86 using their own unordered .find(ADMIN && ACTIVE) instead of selectCurrentUserProfile) remains open and latent — unchanged this pass, still no second-school UserProfile in production to make it live. No RLS, entity, permission, or route-access code touched. Verified: npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm run build, npm run validate:rls (32 entities), npm run test (276/276), npm run test:permissions (23/23), npm run release:gate, npm audit (0 vulnerabilities) all pass, both before and after the fix.

previousBumpRationale_1_7_9: Patch: release-metadata catch-up (weekly automated audit, 2026-08-24). Five real modules shipped on main between 2026-08-18 and 2026-08-23 — module 11 (deploy tooling: app-id binding, deploy:site), module 12 (three-way light/dark/system theme switcher replacing module 10's two-state toggle), the npm run test:smoke live-site suite, module 14 (multi-tenant isolation audit, one latent not-live finding), and module 15 (per-app derived signing key for the Mission Control bridge, closing a shared-secret attribution gap) — and none of them bumped package.json, added a CHANGELOG.md entry, or updated this file / src/lib/appConfig.js's APP_VERSION, which was still reading 1.7.5, three releases stale. This bump closes that gap; see CLAUDE.md for each module's own detailed writeup. Also fixed in this round: react-router/react-router-dom 6.30.4 -> 6.30.6 (npm audit fix, lockfile-only) closing GHSA-jjmj-jmhj-qwj2 — the other two react-router advisories need a v6->v7 major upgrade and remain accepted risk, unchanged from every prior audit (client-only SPA, no SSR, no externally-controlled navigation target). USER_MANUAL.md gained its first mentions of the theme switcher, the HistorialCambios page (module 6), and the danger-zone export/deletion-request actions (module 7) — all live, user-facing, previously undocumented. New docs/security-audit-2026-08-24.md. No RLS, entity, permission, or route-access code changed. previousBumpRationale_1_7_8: Patch: portfolio-standard audit (module 10 — dark theme). tailwind.config.js already had darkMode:['class'] and index.css already had a complete .dark token palette (shadcn boilerplate), but nothing ever applied the .dark class — no toggle, no persisted preference, no prefers-color-scheme fallback. New src/lib/ThemeContext.jsx (ThemeProvider/useTheme, localStorage key 'liuma-theme', resolution order stored preference -> prefers-color-scheme -> light), a matching inline pre-mount script in index.html (avoids a flash of the wrong theme before React hydrates — kept in sync with ThemeContext.jsx by hand, each side comments the other), and a new ThemeToggle component wired into both places a user can reach it: SideNav's identity footer (desktop) and CommandPalette's new footer row (mobile — the bottom nav's 4 slots were already all spoken for, so the palette, opened from the same 'Más' tab, is the only mobile-reachable spot). Six pre-existing hardcoded-light spots (PendingApproval.jsx, ContinueAs.jsx, App.jsx's two loading skeletons, Layout.jsx's footer, PageNotFound.jsx) got matching dark: variants. Four more hardcoded bg-white/text-slate spots (LumiChat.jsx, HomeChrome.jsx, WelcomeTrialModal.jsx, SuspendedAccountModal.jsx, AdminHome.jsx's tenant-switcher pill) were checked and left as-is — all sit on brand-color (bg-primary) or semantic-color (bg-destructive) surfaces already theme-aware via CSS custom properties, or are white-on-color overlay/scrim decoration, not themed neutral page surfaces. Verified: npm run lint, npm run build, npm run validate:rls (32 entities), npm test (276/276) all pass. Visually verified with Playwright (Chromium) against a local dev server — /login (role-picker step) and a 404 page, both in dark mode — text contrast, card/border colors all render correctly. Not verified: any authenticated page — not reachable without live Base44 auth in this environment; risk is bounded since those pages already use the same semantic tokens (bg-card, text-foreground, etc.) the .dark palette in index.css was hand-tuned for.
previousBumpRationale_1_7_7: Patch: portfolio-standard audit (module 7 — cuenta y zona de peligro). PermisosRoles.jsx already rendered a 'Danger Zone' spec table (delete/suspend/reset/transfer tenant) but it was read-only documentation with no working action behind it — no data export, no way to request deletion. New base44/functions/exportSchoolData (service role, but every read explicitly filtered by the caller's own school_id, re-derived server-side from their ACTIVE ADMIN UserProfile, never trusted from the request) returns every row the school owns across 23 operational entities as one JSON payload; PermisosRoles.jsx turns the response into a client-side download. 'Solicitar eliminación de la escuela' is deliberately NOT a direct delete — School.delete's RLS requires role:admin (the ACACIA platform owner), so a school's own ADMIN cannot delete their own school via RLS at all, by design — this creates a SupportTicket (category ACCOUNT, priority HIGH) via the existing createSupportTicket helper, which resolveSupportRouting already always routes to the platform owner for an ADMIN's own tickets regardless of category. The pre-existing 4-operation maker-checker spec table (delete/suspend/reset/transfer) is left as-is, now explicitly labeled as a separate, larger, not-yet-built initiative rather than conflated with the new functional card — building that maker-checker system for real is out of scope for this release, same reasoning as when it was first documented as deferred. No RLS or entity change beyond the new function. Verified: npm run lint, npm run build, npm run validate:rls (32 entities), npm test (276/276) all pass.

previousBumpRationale_1_7_5: Patch, critical security fix: completing 1.7.3's module-4 live deploy (base44/entities/*.jsonc → the actual Base44 backend, via update_entity_schema — a repo commit alone never changes runtime RLS) surfaced that Base44's live RLS engine silently drops any sibling key placed alongside "user_condition" in the same rule object — {"data.school_id": X, "user_condition": Y} evaluates as user_condition ALONE, X is discarded. That shape was already the DEPLOYED form of most tenant-scoping rules across this app (not something 1.7.3 introduced), found via update_entity_schema's own validator while pushing 1.7.3's fix live. Scanned all 32 entities: 29 had it, 84 instances total, almost all on the data.school_id tenant-isolation clause — meaning any user matching the role half of the rule (e.g. data.app_role:ADMIN) could read/write across ALL schools, not just their own, on nearly every entity in the app. Same defect class jospabloh/cateqhub's CLAUDE.md documents finding once in one entity (Parish) with a note it was worth checking elsewhere — this is elsewhere, at much larger scale. Fixed by wrapping every such pair as an explicit {"$and": [{"user_condition":...}, {...rest}]} — semantics preserved exactly, nothing narrowed or widened beyond restoring the intended tenant scoping. Two further live-engine constraints surfaced and fixed while deploying: (1) a nested $or directly inside another $or is not evaluated on WRITE rules (create/update/delete) — "the branch silently matches" — fixed by flattening (read rules tolerate nested $or fine, left as-is); (2) the entity-side built-in record id must be addressed as "id", not "_id" — Classroom/School/Student used "_id" and were rejected on redeploy; renamed. All 29 corrected entities deployed live via the Base44 MCP and re-fetched to confirm. Added a permanent guard for the primary defect: scripts/validate-rls.mjs now flags any rule object mixing user_condition with sibling keys (previously silent — this exact shape passed validate:rls for years since it's syntactically valid Mongo-style implicit-AND, just not how Base44's engine actually evaluates it). No entity field, property, or intended-access rule changed — verified per-entity that `properties`/`required` are byte-identical before/after and every fix is a pure re-expression of the same access the original (broken) rule intended. 276/276 tests pass; scripts/validate-rls.mjs passes clean (32 entities, new check included); lint clean; build succeeds.

architecture.runtime: browser (client-side only; no application server) + Base44 backend functions for privileged mutations
architecture.router: react-router-dom v7 (declarative mode: BrowserRouter/Routes/Route/useNavigate/Link — stable across v6->v7)
architecture.enforcementBoundary: base44 Row-Level Security (entity + field-level RLS) in base44/entities/*.jsonc + service-role backend functions in base44/functions/*
architecture.language: JavaScript / JSX (type-checked via jsconfig); Deno TypeScript for backend functions
